info.name: GK One Identity — QA (dev)
info.description:
Exercises GK One Identity the way an integrating application does: the OAuth 2.1 authorization code flow with PKCE, and the endpoints a token opens.

It is pointed at the **dev** test client. Folders `00` to `04` need nothing filled in; the milestone folders say what they need in their own descriptions.

**Sign in.** Open the collection's **Authorization** tab and press **Get New Access Token**. Postman opens the GK One sign-in window, and the token comes back to it. Press **Use Token**. Nothing here posts a password to an internal endpoint: the sign-in happens where a customer's would.

Folder `01` copies that token into the **accessToken** variable, for the requests that need the raw string. Folder `02` runs the same flow by hand when you want the refresh token captured too, which Postman's helper keeps to itself.

**Milestones 9 to 11.** Each milestone has a folder named after it, and **Milestones 9 to 11 · Sign in first** runs the sign-ins they share. Each request is named after the outcome it checks in *GK One Identity, Milestones 9 to 11*: `M10.7` is outcome 7 of milestone 10. The Milestone 11 folder calls the account page's API with the browser's session cookie, which you copy into a variable; its description says how. Each folder lists the outcomes only a browser or the admin portal can show.

**One refresh token per customer and application.** The last sign-in wins: a sign-in with `clientId` anywhere, the dev test client and Postman's OAuth helper included, ends the refresh token an earlier sign-in captured. A sign-out anywhere for that application ends its access tokens on every browser. A refresh that answers `invalid_grant`, or a `401` on a token that has not expired, means you start that folder's sign-in again.

item.name: 02 · Sign in by hand, to capture the refresh token
item.description:
Postman's OAuth helper keeps the refresh token to itself. This folder runs the same flow request by request so every token lands in a variable.

1. Run **Build the sign-in URL**. It generates the PKCE pair and prints the URL to the Postman console.
2. Open that URL in a browser and sign in.
3. Copy the `code` from the address bar into the `authCode` variable.
4. Run **Exchange code for tokens**.

item.name: Milestones 9 to 11 · Sign in first
item.description:
The sign-ins milestones 9, 10 and 11 share. Run this folder first.

**Setup**
- `clientId` is the dev test client: a GK One application, with **First-party application** on and the API in `apiIdentifier` under **Expose an API**. `redirectUri` is registered on it.
- `thirdPartyClientId` and `thirdPartyClientSecret` name a third-party application: First-party off, `redirectUri` registered, `offline_access` enabled. Ask an operator for one. The requests that need it report SETUP NEEDED until you fill them in.

**Run in this order**
1. Run `00 · Discovery document`. It saves the scope catalogue that M10.2 compares against.
2. Run **M10.2 · Build the sign-in URL**, open the URL from the Postman console in a browser, sign in, and paste the `code` into `fpAuthCode`. Then run the three requests below it.
3. Run **M10.5 · Build the sign-in URL**, sign in the same way, paste its `code` into `tpAuthCode`, and run the exchange below it.

M10.3 and M10.5 are what you see in the browser during these sign-ins: no consent screen for the GK One application, and a consent screen for the third-party one.

item.name: M10.2 · Build the sign-in URL (GK One application)

request.description:
Builds the PKCE pair and prints the `/authorize` URL to the Postman console. Open the URL in a browser, sign in, and paste the `code` from the address bar into `fpAuthCode`.

item.name: Milestone 9 · Legacy IAM token bridge
item.description:

**Setup**
- `apimSubscriptionKey`: the APIM subscription key the existing `/api` endpoints and gkone-core need. The two M9.1 requests that call them report SETUP NEEDED until you fill it in.
- The third-party requests, M9.3 and M9.5, need the third-party sign-in from **Sign in first**.

item.name: M9.9 · More than 60 a minute (Runner, 121 iterations)
item.description:
Run this subfolder alone in the Collection Runner, with **121** iterations and no delay. 121 requests in under a minute put more than 60 into one of the fixed one-minute windows, wherever the run starts.

The limit counts every `/token` request of this application, so for up to a minute afterwards its sign-ins and refreshes answer `429` too. Run it when nobody else is using the dev test client, or point `clientId` at a client of your own.

item.name: Milestone 11 · Account page
item.description:
Milestone 11's rules, through the calls the account page makes. Each call takes the customer's GK One session in the body, as `sessionToken`.

**Copy the session.** In a browser, sign in at `/account` on the sign-in host, the address in `loginBase` (`https://app-gkone-identity-001-dev.azurewebsites.net/account` in dev). Open the developer tools, then **Application → Cookies** for that address, and copy the value of `__Host-gkone-session` into `sessionToken`. For M11.2 and M11.3, sign in from a second browser or a private window too, and copy its cookie into `sessionTokenB`. Either cookie signs in as that customer: clear both variables when you finish, and keep them out of any export you share.

**Before you start**
- Sign in with `clientId` once, through **Milestones 9 to 11 · Sign in first** or the dev test client, so a GK One application is listed.
- For M11.6 and M11.7, sign in with the third-party application through M10.5 in that same folder.

**Run top to bottom.** The reads and refusals come first. Then M11.3 ends browser B's sessions, M11.5 ends every other session, M11.7 removes the third-party application, and M11.4 ends this browser's own session, which signs it out.

**Checked in the browser, not here:** the cards, the five rows per card, **View all** and the header tabs (M11.1); the grouping by operating system and browser and the **This device** label (M11.2); the **Keep this session** and **End this session too** dialog (M11.4); and the confirmation before **Remove access** (M11.7).
